title: Agri-Meteorological Data
topic: soil moisture deficit and soil drainage classes
notes: Explains the Soil Moisture Deficit model and distinguishes well-drained, moderately drained and poorly drained soils. Use as supporting evidence for drainage-sensitive scenarios; do not treat regional values as exact field-level observations.

title: How to protect soils from the impact of machinery
topic: soil moisture, machinery weight and soil compaction
scope: Irish agricultural field operations; article primarily discusses tillage machinery
notes: Supports relationships between wet soil, axle load, ground pressure and compaction. Its underlying soil principles are relevant, but scenarios should not imply that every tillage recommendation automatically applies to dairy grassland.

title: Spring Grazing Management
topic: spring grazing, ground conditions and paddock selection
notes: Supports direct paddock assessment, selecting suitable paddocks and adjusting grazing according to ground conditions. Relevant to turnout, poaching-risk and insufficient-context scenarios.

title: Wet weather management techniques back in play
scope: Irish pasture-based livestock and dairy systems
notes: Supports practices such as twelve-hour allocations, back fencing and on-off grazing during difficult wet conditions. Use for scenarios comparing unrestricted access with managed grazing.

title: Unlocking the potential of heavy soils dairy farms
topic: heavy soils, grazing infrastructure and paddock-level management
scope: Irish dairy farms with moderately or poorly drained soils
notes: Explains that standard dairy-management principles may require adjustment during prolonged wet weather and poor grazing conditions. Supports scenarios involving heavy soils, roadways, access points and paddock-level variation.

title: Soil Drainage
topic: soil drainage assessment and drainage-system selection
notes: Emphasises that drainage challenges vary by soil and site and require investigation rather than a single universal solution. Useful for missing-context and local-variation scenarios.

title: Grassland management and clover
notes: Provides the wider project context that Irish dairy production is strongly based on converting grazed pasture into milk. Use for project framing rather than individual risk labels.

title: Finding a suitable soil moisture range for safe field operations in grassland
topic: soil moisture and safe machinery traffic on grassland
scope: Managed temperate grassland, including Irish field operations
notes: Supports the relationship between soil moisture, rainfall timing, heavy machinery and soil structural damage. Any numerical thresholds should be represented with their stated context and should not be converted into universal rules.
